title: Часы над Мерсер-стрит: удержать смысл целой статьи
subtitle: Длинное чтение, конкурирующая память и решения, которые нельзя вывести из фотографии
units: Авторский практикум · законченная статья и новый перенос
goal: Прочитать целый сложный текст, восстановить связи между удалёнными частями, оценить разные свидетельства, подготовить адресный вывод и пересмотреть его после нового источника.
formula: claim → source and scope → distant connection → audience-specific synthesis → revision

sections.title: Первый проход: держать весь вопрос
sections.body: Длинный текст требует памяти о ходе мысли. На первом проходе не останавливайся у каждого выражения: после нескольких абзацев запиши короткую рабочую формулировку вопроса и отметь, что заставило её изменить. Здесь начало, эпизод с магазином и финал связаны через ошибочный образ остановившейся жизни. Понимание отдельного абзаца ещё не объясняет эту связь. Прочитай статью целиком, затем вернись к помеченным местам. Словарь используй для слова, без которого меняется вывод, а не для каждого непривычного оборота.

sections.title: Дальние связи: источник, голос и граница
sections.body: Различай автора статьи, героя, старый документ, черновик подписи и нового редактора. Все они могут говорить об одном предмете, но отвечать на разные вопросы. Выпиши утверждение, укажи его автора и найди позднюю деталь, которая ограничивает, поддерживает или переосмысливает его. Поздняя оговорка не обязательно опровергает раннее высказывание. Иногда она лишь уточняет период, группу людей или объект сравнения. Хорошая аргументация сохраняет полезное свидетельство даже после того, как из него убрали слишком широкий вывод.

sections.title: Риторика: не путать силу образа с фактом
sections.body: Повторяющийся образ может объединять статью и одновременно скрывать различия. Вопрос читателя: что именно делает эта формулировка — создаёт общий образ, подчёркивает иронию, переключает перспективу или сообщает проверяемое событие? Для ответа нужны место в статье и соседние факты. Слова everyone и whole town не всегда обозначают результат подсчёта; в воспоминании они могут быть эмоциональным обобщением. Объясни такую функцию, сохранив возможность другого чтения и не объявляя неустановленное намерение автора доказанным.

sections.title: Медиация и пересмотр без потери результата
sections.body: Для редактора важен сквозной аргумент, для правления — решения и проверка условий. Создай два самостоятельных текста, каждый под своего адресата. Не пересказывай пятнадцать абзацев по очереди: выбери связи, которые помогают выполнить задачу. После позднего сообщения проверь, какое предложение собственного ответа действительно нужно заменить, какое лишь уточнить и какое сохранить. Пересмотр не требует выбрасывать все прежние данные. В новом независимом случае переноси способ анализа, а не имена, цифры и готовую рекомендацию предыдущего проекта.

examples.en: The interview supports a particular memory; it does not establish how every resident used the clock.
examples.ru: Интервью подтверждает конкретное воспоминание, но не устанавливает, как часами пользовался каждый житель.
examples.why: Сохраняем свидетельство и ограничиваем охват вывода.

examples.en: A moving dial would be a visible result, although it would not by itself constitute a restoration of the original mechanism.
examples.ru: Движущийся циферблат был бы видимым результатом, хотя сам по себе не означал бы восстановления исходного механизма.
examples.why: Различаем два результата, не обесценивая первый.

examples.en: The grocery-store photograph complicates the opening image rather than merely adding another date.
examples.ru: Фотография магазина усложняет начальный образ, а не просто добавляет ещё одну дату.
examples.why: Объясняем дальнюю смысловую связь между частями текста.

examples.en: I would narrow the claim about Roy’s memory while retaining the fact that he supports a working bell.
examples.ru: Я бы сузил утверждение о воспоминании Роя, сохранив факт, что он поддерживает работающий колокол.
examples.why: Пересмотр относится к конкретному утверждению, а не ко всей позиции человека.

materials.title: The Clock Above Mercer Street — полный оригинальный текст
materials.text:
The Clock Above Mercer Street

[1]
At nine seventeen, the clock above Mercer Street was doing what it had done for fifteen years: declining to take sides between morning and evening. Below it, a delivery driver checked his phone and double-parked beside the former machine shop. There was enough confusion to spoil the old joke. Its two faces showed different hours. From the river, it was always twenty past three. From the street, it was nine seventeen. Neither face had moved since a power failure in January 2011. That fact was available in a maintenance folder at the Pine Bend Historical Center. I had nevertheless written, in a newspaper caption the previous spring, that the hands had stopped when the mill closed. The mill had closed in 1998. A picturesque sentence had carried me thirteen years away from the record.

[2]
I returned to Pine Bend, a small Wisconsin town, because the historical center wanted to make the clock run again. A donor had offered to cover a preliminary inspection. Posters showed a bright face against the dark brick tower. Across the bottom, the campaign asked residents to help restore the clock that had kept time for everyone. I liked the photograph. I liked the sentence less, though it was close to something I might have written. When I asked the curator, Lena Quinn, what everyone meant, she did not produce a definition. She turned the poster over. A volunteer had penciled three questions on the back: Which mechanism? Which hour? Whose story? The public campaign had begun before the center had settled those questions.

[3]
The clock was installed in 1926, thirty-eight years after the mill opened. A company newsletter described it as a gift to the town. Employees had paid part of the cost through small weekly contributions; the surviving announcement did not say whether those contributions were voluntary. The newsletter thanked the director by name and the workforce as a group. Lena would not call that proof of coercion. Nor would she describe the mechanism as a purely generous donation. She placed the announcement beside a payroll list and asked what each could establish. One recorded a public claim, the other a deduction. Neither recorded how a particular worker had felt. We are used to treating an old document as a firm surface beneath slippery memory. Here, two firm surfaces did not meet.

[4]
Roy Bell, who had worked nights in the finishing room from 1971 until the closure, remembered the clock as a sound. From his station, he could not see either face. He heard the bell at the end of a shift and, in earlier years, while walking home along the river. In a recorded interview at the center, he said that the whole town used to listen. The remark had become the exhibition's most frequently quoted line. When I played it back, Roy smiled at himself. He had meant the people he walked home with, he said, and the neighbors awake at that hour. He did not mean he had conducted a survey. He still wanted the bell restored. Correcting the reach of his claim had not weakened the attachment behind it.

[5]
Anika Torres brought a different measure of time. She had scheduled deliveries between 1976 and 1989 and still had a notebook of bus departures. The tower clock, she said, was not what decided whether someone was late. A separate punch clock stood inside the east entrance. Delivery appointments were written on a wall chart, and supervisors occasionally adjusted the sequence when a truck broke down. Anika remembered the tower being set five minutes ahead for several months, so that people would leave the lunchroom early enough to reach their stations. She could date the practice only to the late seventies. She did not remember whether both faces had been advanced. A clock could be useful, she suggested, without being neutral. Then she asked me not to turn that thought into an accusation about unpaid work.

[6]
I found three daily sheets from 1978 showing lunch breaks that ended five minutes before the hour. Those sheets did not establish why the breaks ended then, whether the tower was fast, or how anyone's pay was calculated. They also did not make Anika's recollection worthless. The problem was one of fit: the sheets addressed scheduling; her memory addressed a signal people followed; my question had drifted toward fairness. Lena proposed recording all three separately. A draft display label did exactly the opposite. It said that the clock had disciplined workers for half a century. The sentence had force, but its duration came from nowhere. It replaced one tidy collective story with another. We crossed it out together, without deciding that discipline had therefore played no part in the mill's life.

[7]
The tower itself offered less certainty than its solid outline suggested. Caleb Price, a clock repairer, climbed with us through a narrow hatch and opened a cabinet with a modern padlock. Behind it were gears from the original mechanism, an electric motor fitted in the 1960s, and a controller installed in 1994. A visitor looking up from the sidewalk saw an old clock. Inside, age was distributed unevenly. Caleb could make the street face move using a new electric drive while leaving much of the earlier mechanism untouched. Restoring the surviving mechanical system would require a fuller examination, replacement parts, and a person willing to maintain it. He declined to name a completion date. A working face and a restored historic mechanism, he explained, were different deliverables, even if a photograph made them look identical.

[8]
The campaign's organizer, Martin Vale, worried that distinctions would exhaust the donors. People wanted to see the hands move, he said, and every new qualification made the project sound further away. He was not arguing for a false label. He wanted the center to begin with a visible result and use the attention to support the slower work. The inspection gift did not pay for either restoration option, and no construction contract had been signed. On the campaign page, however, a volunteer had changed could run next summer to will run next summer. Martin had missed the edit. When Lena showed it to him, he restored the conditional language himself. His impatience with uncertainty had not made him indifferent to a promise. The distinction mattered, because an easy villain would have made my article easier too.

[9]
Across the street, Noor Patel was stacking fruit outside the grocery store her parents opened in 2004. The mill had been empty before her family arrived. She supported repairing the tower because loose pieces of trim had closed part of the sidewalk twice that winter. She had no particular preference about the hands. The posters made the town's most important shared experience sound like one she could only borrow. Did she have to acquire someone else's nostalgia to belong here? she asked. Then she pointed to the clock in a photograph of the store's first summer. It had been running above their opening banner. The same object that supposedly marked the end of town life had quietly accompanied the beginning of hers. My old caption had erased that interval as efficiently as it had misdated a breakdown.

[10]
The historical center held sixty-two recorded mill interviews. That sounded substantial until Lena described how the collection had grown. Most interviews had come through two reunion groups. Retired office staff and people who remained nearby were easier to contact than temporary workers or families who had moved away. Eleven interviewees were women, and none had arrived in Pine Bend after the mill closed to work in its newer businesses. These facts did not invalidate the interviews or make the missing accounts predictable. They changed the questions the center could reasonably answer with them. Sixty-two witnesses could provide sixty-two valuable accounts without representing a town. Lena had started a list of possible new contacts. A list was not a completed collection, and she was careful not to advertise the intended range as a range already achieved.

[11]
At an open meeting, residents were invited to put stickers beside three pictures: a running clock, a conserved but stationary mechanism, and an empty tower. Fifty-four people used the board. Thirty-one chose the running clock, seventeen the stationary mechanism, and six the empty tower. The exercise gave the organizers a useful opening for conversation. It did not resolve what running meant, whether the bell should sound at night, or how maintenance would be funded. Attendance had been advertised through the historical center's mailing list and a notice in the grocery store. Martin began to say that the town had chosen restoration, then stopped and said that most people who used the board had preferred a running clock. Several people applauded the shorter first version anyway. Precision does not always arrive at the moment an audience is ready to hear it.

[12]
One resident, Dana Brooks, asked whether the bell could be switched off after ten. She worked an early shift at a distribution center outside town and slept with a window open in summer. Roy initially heard her question as a request to remove the bell altogether. She repeated it, this time naming the hours she wanted quiet. He nodded. They did not reach an agreement about a schedule, but they stopped arguing over two different proposals. Watching them, I realized that the question of whose time the clock kept had a present tense. The dispute did not require one person to love history and another to dislike it. A restored sound could give one resident a connection and another a reason to close a window. Both effects could occur even if the engineering work was impeccable.

[13]
Lena's revised display would keep the 1926 announcement, Anika's interview, and Roy's recording in separate panels, with dates and brief notes about what remained uncertain. She also wanted to include the grocery-store photograph. That addition would not convert the collection into a complete account of Pine Bend. It would interrupt the suggestion that history had finished at the mill gate. She asked whether we should remove the campaign's phrase for everyone. I thought we should replace it, but Roy disagreed. Keep it as a question, he suggested. Had it kept time for everyone? Who could see it, who heard it, and who had been expected to obey it? He was not withdrawing his wish to hear the bell. He was making room for a wish that did not need to speak in everybody else's name.

[14]
Before I left, Caleb set a small temporary dial on a workbench and connected it to his test equipment. Its hands moved smoothly. No one in the room mistook that success for a finished tower. It demonstrated that one proposed drive could move a dial under those conditions; it did not answer the questions about weather exposure, the second face, historic parts, sound, or long-term care. Still, it was progress. The danger in admitting limits is that a writer can become so determined to avoid exaggeration that nothing is allowed to count. I had nearly done that to Martin's campaign. A result does not have to settle an entire argument to be worth reporting. The obligation is to say what it settles, and to resist borrowing the authority of the questions it leaves open.

[15]
In my new draft, I corrected the closure date and the date of the power failure. I did not replace the first caption with a story about a town recovering its lost identity. Pine Bend had been working on several identities while the hands stood still. The article ended with Noor unlocking the store, Roy checking the bus schedule, and Dana leaving for her early shift. None of those scenes, taken alone, could stand for everyone. Together they suggested why the tower mattered without assigning it one uncontested meaning. At nine seventeen, the street face remained still. For the moment, its most useful service was making people specify which time they meant. Whether it would soon tell the time again depended on decisions the photograph could not make for them.

materials.title: Задание редакции и правления
materials.text:
Editorial commission — fictional local-history magazine
Your editor wants a complete argument about the restoration debate, not a tourism advertisement. Readers know nothing about Pine Bend. Use the article as the only source of established facts. Explain what restoring the clock could mean, whose accounts are represented, and what remains undecided. A recommendation may support progress while requiring accurate public wording. Do not estimate costs, promise a date, or invent residents' consent. The board of the historical center will also read a shorter practical brief. It needs decisions to make before commissioning work and one realistic way to improve the evidence base. The narrator's caption and the campaign's premature promise are different mistakes by different people.

materials.title: Поздняя проверка записи — открыть перед e7
materials.text:
Late interview note — open only before e7
Lena: We checked the original audio after Roy called. The recording used in the exhibition cuts out the sentence immediately before “the whole town used to listen.” In that sentence, Roy said he was thinking about a winter in 1973 when his usual bus was not running. The excerpt did not invent his words, but it removed a time frame that matters. Roy still wants a working bell. He does not agree that this newly recovered sentence proves that nobody listened at other times. He has agreed to a new label that identifies the particular memory and links to the complete interview.
Martin: I also need to correct the meeting report. The fifty-four stickers were placed by fifty-four different attendees; we checked that. We still do not have a count of everyone who attended, and the vote was not advertised as a town survey. Please do not remove the figures, but do not give them a denominator we cannot support.
These notes add fictional source information; they are not evidence about any real restoration project.

materials.title: Независимый случай: архив радиостанции
materials.text:
Independent case for delayed transfer — all facts are fictional
A small community radio station proposes replaying recordings of its 1980s evening music show. The archive contains eighteen complete programs, all selected and donated by the former host. A volunteer describes them as “the soundtrack every teenager grew up with.” The station has no audience research from that period. Two former listeners remember the show warmly. One teenager from the same period says she could not receive the station in her neighborhood and listened to a different service.
A test confirmed that the studio can play digital files. No broadcast permission or launch date has been confirmed. The host supports the project but wants his old introductions preserved, including occasional mistakes, with present-day context added separately. A current student wants to interview people who were not listeners. The station has offered an interview slot, but nobody has yet accepted an invitation.
Your task is an internal recommendation about how to present the proposed series accurately. You are not being asked to resolve copyright: identify that permission is still required rather than inventing its outcome. Do not import Pine Bend's clock, figures, residents, or proposed engineering options into this case.

exercises.prompt: Первый полный проход, 15–20 минут. Прочитайте m1 от начала до конца, не открывая m2–m4 и образцы. Для редактора напишите 120–160 английских слов: какой вопрос постепенно занимает место простого вопроса о ремонте часов? Покажите два поворота рассуждения из разных частей и объясните позицию рассказчика к финалу. Не делайте по одному предложению на каждый абзац.
exercises.context: Авторский учебный материал. Все люди, место и события вымышлены. Сначала собственная попытка, затем образец. Разные обоснованные формулировки допустимы.
answers: The article begins with a visible defect but develops into a question about whose experience a restored clock would represent. The narrator first corrects a caption that confused the mill’s closure with a later power failure. That apparently small correction becomes more significant when Noor’s photograph shows the clock accompanying a new business after the mill had closed. A second turn comes when the meeting exposes different present-day needs: Roy wants the bell, while Dana wants quiet at particular hours. The issue therefore extends beyond preserving a shared past. By the end, the narrator supports reporting limited progress, such as the successful test of a dial, without presenting it as a complete solution. The final position is neither simple nostalgia nor a rejection of restoration; it calls for specific claims and decisions that recognize different accounts.
exercises.hint: Ищите не тему каждого абзаца, а то, как меняется основной вопрос.
exercises.explanation: Сильный ответ связывает начало, магазин, встречу и финальный тест общей мыслью. Перечень персонажей сам по себе не показывает движения аргумента. Рассказчик признаёт ошибку красивой подписи, но не делает обратного вывода, будто любой ремонт или воспоминание бесполезны. В четырнадцатом абзаце он прямо защищает право сообщать ограниченный успех. Поэтому итог может поддерживать проект условно, одновременно требуя точности. Другой выбор двух поворотов допустим, если объяснена их функция и связь с концом.

exercises.prompt: Проверка дальних связей, 10 минут. Напишите 150–190 английских слов для коллеги-редактора. Свяжите P1 с P9 и P15: назовите две разные даты и объясните, что ошибка подписи стирала помимо календарной точности. Затем свяжите P7 с P14: что именно подтвердил тест, а чего он не подтвердил? Укажите номера абзацев и минимум четыре точные фактические опоры.
exercises.context: Авторский учебный материал. Все люди, место и события вымышлены. Сначала собственная попытка, затем образец. Разные обоснованные формулировки допустимы.
answers: P1 separates the mill’s closure in 1998 from the power failure in January 2011. The narrator’s old caption collapsed those events into a single symbolic ending. P9 shows why that matters beyond chronology: Noor’s family opened its grocery store in 2004, and their opening photograph includes the still-running clock. The caption therefore overlooked a period of new activity rather than simply getting a date wrong. P15 returns to this problem by presenting several current lives without making any one stand for the whole town. P7 and P14 establish a different distinction. Inside the tower, parts from several periods coexist, so moving a face is not equivalent to restoring the surviving historic mechanism. The workbench test in P14 shows that one proposed drive can move a temporary dial under test conditions. It does not establish weather performance, operation of the second face, a bell schedule, or future maintenance. Both pairs of passages warn against letting a visible image claim more than its evidence supports.
exercises.hint: Сначала разделите события и результаты, затем объясните, почему различие важно.
exercises.explanation: Нужны две причинно-смысловые связи, а не четыре независимых цитаты. Магазин появился между закрытием и поломкой, поэтому неверная подпись делает новую жизнь невидимой. Технический тест имеет другой предмет: возможность движения одного циферблата в заданных условиях. Он не доказывает состояние исторических деталей и согласованность звукового режима. Не называй тест неудачным: движение состоялось. Точное ограничение делает результат пригодным для решения, а не отменяет его.

exercises.prompt: Свидетельства и позиции, 10 минут. Для куратора напишите 150–190 английских слов: сопоставьте P3, P4–P6 и P10–P11. Объясните, что позволяют утверждать взнос работников, воспоминание Аники, коллекция интервью и 54 наклейки. Выберите два случая, где сильный вывод не поддержан. Сохраните полезность источников; не называйте отсутствие доказательства доказательством противоположного.
exercises.context: Авторский учебный материал. Все люди, место и события вымышлены. Сначала собственная попытка, затем образец. Разные обоснованные формулировки допустимы.
answers: The payroll list supports the fact that workers contributed to the clock, while the newsletter records the company’s public presentation of the gift. Neither establishes whether a particular worker contributed willingly. Anika’s recollection is evidence of how she remembers a signal being used, but the three surviving scheduling sheets do not confirm the tower’s setting or a pay practice. Calling the clock an instrument of discipline for half a century would therefore outrun the evidence. The interview collection remains valuable because it preserves individual accounts; its recruitment through reunion groups nevertheless limits any claim that it represents Pine Bend as a whole. Similarly, the sticker board records preferences among fifty-four participants in one exercise. Thirty-one preferred a running clock, but the exercise did not define the mechanism or establish a town-wide mandate. These limitations call for more precise labels and further questions, not the rejection of memories, documents, or the meeting itself.
exercises.hint: Для каждого утверждения проверьте группу, период, показатель и способ получения сведений.
exercises.explanation: Разные источники отвечают на разные вопросы. Платёжная ведомость не сообщает согласие работника, расписание не устанавливает расчёт зарплаты, число интервью не устраняет способ отбора. Наклейки полезны как наблюдение о конкретном упражнении, но не как доказательство позиции всех жителей. Можно оспорить другие два чрезмерных вывода, если ответ явно показывает недостающую связь. Недопустимо заменять «не доказано принуждение» на «все платили добровольно» или отсутствие интервью новых жителей на догадку об их единой позиции.

exercises.prompt: Риторика и лексика, 8 минут. Напишите 130–170 английских слов для редакционного семинара. Объясните по контексту три выражения: “declining to take sides” в P1, “age was distributed unevenly” в P7 и “making room for a wish” в P13. Для каждого дайте прямую перифразу и объясните его роль. Затем предложите одно собственное предложение с одним из выражений в новой вымышленной ситуации; не переносите часы.
exercises.context: Авторский учебный материал. Все люди, место и события вымышлены. Сначала собственная попытка, затем образец. Разные обоснованные формулировки допустимы.
answers: In P1, “declining to take sides” personifies the stopped clock: it cannot distinguish morning from evening, rather than literally choosing neutrality. The playful opening also introduces the article’s concern with competing perspectives. In P7, “age was distributed unevenly” means that the clock contains components installed in different periods. It challenges the simple visual impression of one uniformly old object. In P13, “making room for a wish” means allowing Roy’s desire for the bell to coexist with other needs without presenting his preference as universal. The spatial image turns an apparently weaker claim into a more inclusive one. A new context might be: “By adding a quiet study room, the school was making room for a wish that the busy group schedule had overlooked.” Here, too, making room refers both to practical provision and to recognizing a previously neglected preference.
exercises.hint: Не переводите отдельные слова: объясните, какую работу выражение делает в аргументе.
exercises.explanation: Перифраза должна передать значение выражения именно в статье. У часов нет политической позиции: это олицетворение, связанное с неподвижностью и дальнейшими разногласиями. Возраст распределён между деталями разных лет, а не между жителями. В третьем случае речь идёт о совместимости частной просьбы с чужими потребностями. Собственный пример проверяет перенос значения; он не обязан повторять тему истории или содержать все три выражения. Объяснение эффекта может быть иным, если опирается на контекст.

exercises.prompt: Самостоятельная аргументация, 15 минут. Теперь откройте m2. Напишите для местного журнала статью-ответ 260–320 английских слов с собственным заголовком. Защитите позицию о том, как стоит представить восстановление часов публике. Обязательно соедините техническое различие P7/P14, историческое свидетельство P3–P6 и современную перспективу P9/P12. Представьте сильную версию довода Мартина и ответьте на неё. Не выдумывайте смету, договор или дату запуска.
exercises.context: Авторский учебный материал. Все люди, место и события вымышлены. Сначала собственная попытка, затем образец. Разные обоснованные формулировки допустимы.
answers:
Let the Clock Tell More Than One Story

Pine Bend can support visible progress on its tower without pretending that either the machine or the town has a single past. The campaign should explain what work it is proposing and let different accounts remain distinct. A more qualified description need not be a less engaging one.

The technical distinction is essential. The tower contains components from several periods, and a new drive could make a face move without restoring the surviving mechanical system. The successful workbench test is worth reporting, but it is evidence about a dial under test conditions. It supplies neither a launch date nor an answer about sound and maintenance.

Historical interpretation needs similar care. Employee contributions complicate the company’s description of a gift, but the surviving records do not establish individual consent. Anika’s account raises a question about time as a workplace signal without proving a particular pay practice. Displaying those sources separately would invite inquiry without replacing a celebratory myth with an equally unsupported accusation.

Martin’s strongest point is that a visible result can attract attention and sustain slower work. A campaign burdened with every unresolved detail may lose its audience. The answer is therefore a clear description of a limited first result, not an indefinite refusal to begin.

The public story should also include people whose lives continued or began after the closure. Noor’s opening photograph and Dana’s request for quiet hours show why belonging and present-day use cannot be settled by nostalgia. Roy’s support for the bell can remain part of that story without speaking for every resident. The center should publish the option it is exploring, identify the decisions still open, and invite accounts beyond its existing reunion networks.
exercises.hint: Начните с собственной ограниченной позиции, затем выбирайте доказательства под неё.
exercises.explanation: Это законченный ответ со своей позицией, а не обзор всех пятнадцати абзацев. Обязательные три линии связаны принципом точного публичного обещания: технический результат, исторический смысл и нынешнее использование требуют разных оснований. Довод Мартина представлен в сильной форме — видимый успех может поддержать дальнейшую работу. Ответ не приписывает ему намерение обмануть. Допустимо рекомендовать другое направление проекта, но нужны те же границы: подарок оплачивает осмотр, дата и контракт не согласованы, предпочтения участников не равны единому решению города.

exercises.prompt: Рабочая медиация, 12 минут. Не открывая m3, напишите правлению исторического центра самостоятельный brief 180–230 английских слов. Правление не читало вашу статью. Назовите ближайшее решение, три разных вопроса, которые оно не решает автоматически, и один выполнимый шаг по расширению свидетельств. Включите точные результаты наклеек с подходящей группой сравнения. Завершите предлагаемой публичной формулировкой, сохраняющей неизвестную дату.
exercises.context: Авторский учебный материал. Все люди, место и события вымышлены. Сначала собственная попытка, затем образец. Разные обоснованные формулировки допустимы.
answers:
The board should first decide which outcome it is asking a specialist to assess: making a clock face run or restoring the surviving historical mechanism. Those are different projects. The preliminary inspection gift and the successful test of a temporary dial do not establish funding for either option or a completion date.

That choice would not automatically settle three further questions: how the historic components should be treated, when the bell should sound, and who will maintain the installation. Roy’s wish for a bell and Dana’s request for quiet hours need to be discussed as distinct, potentially compatible preferences.

The meeting exercise offers a useful starting point, not a town-wide decision. Of fifty-four people who used the sticker board, thirty-one selected a running clock, seventeen a stationary mechanism, and six an empty tower. Running was not defined precisely enough to choose a technical option.

To broaden the evidence base, the center could invite interviews through current businesses and contacts beyond the two reunion groups. Noor’s photograph would add a documented post-closure perspective, while new interviews should remain an invitation until completed.

Suggested public wording: “We are examining options for the tower clock and inviting accounts of its place in Pine Bend. No restoration option or completion date has yet been confirmed.”
exercises.hint: Сократите историю до решений и условий, которые нужны именно правлению.
exercises.explanation: Рабочий brief должен быть полезен человеку без всей статьи. Он различает выбор результата, уход за историческими деталями, расписание звука и обслуживание. Числа наклеек относятся к людям, участвовавшим в упражнении; исходный материал до m3 не устанавливает общее число всех посетителей встречи. Новый контакт или приглашение не считается уже собранным свидетельством. Публичная фраза допускает движение проекта, но не превращает осмотр или тест в оплату и завершение работ. Другая организация допустима при сохранении этих смысловых границ.

exercises.prompt: Поздний источник, 8 минут. Только теперь откройте m3. Произнесите редактору ответ 130–170 английских слов, примерно 75–100 секунд. Объясните, какую конкретную формулировку о Рое следует уточнить, что остаётся верным и чего новая запись не доказывает. Затем решите, как обращаться с цифрами встречи. Запишите речь или её текст; текстовая версия проверяет формулировки, запись дополнительно позволяет прослушать подачу. Это сценарная репетиция, а не живой разговор.
exercises.context: Авторский учебный материал. Все люди, место и события вымышлены. Сначала собственная попытка, затем образец. Разные обоснованные формулировки допустимы.
answers:
I would revise the description of Roy’s recorded memory to identify the winter in 1973 and the disruption to his usual bus. The isolated quotation made the memory sound less specifically situated than the complete recording allows. That is a reason to restore the context and link to the full interview, not to claim that Roy invented the words or that nobody listened in other years. His support for a working bell also remains unchanged.

I would retain the sticker figures. The new check confirms that fifty-four different people placed them, so we should not suggest that a few attendees voted repeatedly. However, we still cannot report the proportion of all meeting attendees, because that total is unknown. The appropriate comparison remains the fifty-four participants in the board exercise. These are targeted revisions: they improve attribution and scope without erasing useful evidence.
exercises.hint: Пересматривайте конкретное утверждение: источник, период, числитель, знаменатель.
exercises.explanation: Новое сообщение не подтверждает удобную противоположность старой истории. Уточняется конкретный зимний контекст Роя; желание восстановить колокол остаётся. Нельзя обвинять запись в выдуманных словах: слова подлинные, удалён контекст. Проверка наклеек устраняет сомнение о повторном голосовании, но не добавляет неизвестный знаменатель всех посетителей. Хороший ответ говорит, какие предложения изменить, а какие сохранить. В тексте оценивается смысл; плавность, интонация и слышимая реакция требуют реальной аудиозаписи и не выводятся из правильной расшифровки.

exercises.prompt: Отсроченный перенос: через 24–48 часов откройте только m4 и это задание, не перечитывая свои ответы про часы. Напишите руководителю радиостанции внутреннюю рекомендацию 180–230 английских слов. Объясните, как описать коллекцию, как представить воспоминания и технический тест, что нужно проверить до объявления запуска и как включить отсутствовавшую перспективу. Включите одну готовую публичную фразу. Все необходимые факты есть в m4; не переносите детали Pine Bend.
exercises.context: Авторский учебный материал. Все люди, место и события вымышлены. Сначала собственная попытка, затем образец. Разные обоснованные формулировки допустимы.
answers:
The proposed series should be presented as eighteen surviving programs selected by their former host, not as the soundtrack of every teenager’s life. The selection is valuable but cannot establish universal reach, particularly when one former teenager recalls being unable to receive the station. Her account does not invalidate the two listeners’ warm memories; it makes the boundaries of those memories clearer.

The host’s original introductions should be distinguishable from present-day commentary. Preserving occasional mistakes can serve a historical purpose if listeners can tell what was said then and what the station knows now. We should discuss that presentation with the host without implying that broadcast permission has already been secured.

The studio test confirms that digital files can be played. It does not establish permission to broadcast them or a launch date. Those matters need confirmation before an announcement promising a series.

I recommend using the offered interview slot to seek accounts from nonlisteners and neighborhoods with different reception. The student’s proposal is a practical next step, but no completed interview should be advertised yet.

A suitable public description would be: “We are exploring a series based on a former host’s archive and inviting different memories of local radio; broadcasting arrangements are not yet confirmed.”
exercises.hint: Ищите те же отношения в новых фактах; оставьте прежние имена и числа за пределами ответа.
exercises.explanation: Независимый случай проверяет перенос способа чтения, а не воспроизведение готового вывода про часы. Восемнадцать программ отобраны одним человеком; это ограничивает охват, но не делает материал бесполезным. Два воспоминания и один опыт отсутствия приёма могут сосуществовать. Тест воспроизведения отделён от разрешения и даты. Запланированное интервью ещё не состоялось. Смысловая ошибка — добавить сюда 54 участника, исторический механизм или решение о колоколе. После ответа сравни критерии и отметь одну реальную сильную сторону и один предел своего переноса.
